summary: Rupert Gethin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester (~1982–1987) under Lance S. Cousins. He became Co-Director of Bristol's Centre for Buddhist Studies (~1987) and President of the Pali Text Society (2003).

Ruriko Sakuma works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Nagoya University, she held posts as a permanent researcher and director at the Eastern Institute and as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, both attested in 2015.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Chicago (~1910–1913). She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America (~1945–1967) and abbess of Ryōsen-an (~1958–1967).

Ruth Gamble specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the Australian National University (ending 2014) supervised by John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman. She held posts at ANU and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2016).

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983 and studied under Jinbo Shi (1987–1988). She became James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.

Ryan Anningson specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under the doctoral supervision of Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University, studying under Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and L. S. Summer, among others.

Ryan Richard Overbey works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Brown University (AB, 2001) and Harvard University (PhD, 2010). His appointments include UC Berkeley (2013–2015), Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Holy Cross, and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2015–2020) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1928–1933) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1941), where he also lectured. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1957–1978).
Ryoichi Kondo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryojin Soga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Toyo University (~1916–1924) and Otani University (~1925–1967), and served as president of the Otani Society (~1961–1967).

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryoko Mochizuki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1963). She served as a lecturer at Rissho University, with posts attested in 1972 and 1983.

Ryosaburo Sakaki worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1893–1895), he lectured at Ryukoku University (1897) and became a professor at Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1956–1960). He was a professor (~1980–2007) and professor emeritus (~2007–2021) at Taisho University, and held posts at Shuchiin University and Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014).

Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He held positions as a researcher at the Soto Zen Administration Research Institute and as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 1998).

Ryosho Hayashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1948–1952) and Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1953–1958). He later served as president of Taisho University (~1991–1995).

Ryosho Tanaka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University (~1952–1960). He held posts at Komazawa University (~1965–1978; professor ~1978–2003) and served as a professor at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Kouda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1998) and at the Hasegawa Institute for Buddhist Culture (attested 2006).
